name: SDLC workflow
description: Plan, implement, and verify a software change from a request. Resolve the target repository and task artifacts, pause for unresolved human decisions, and require a fresh-context final review. Finish locally by default, with optional PR creation.

repoPath.description: Optional target Git checkout. If omitted, the executing agent resolves its current project and records its absolute path.
repoPath.title: Repository path

request.description: What change to make and why, in the requester's words.
request.title: Change request

taskDir.description: Optional project-relative artifact directory. If omitted, reuse the matching task or choose .tasks/<outcome-slug> using repository guidance.
taskDir.title: Artifact directory

reviewPolicy.description: auto asks for human input when material decisions remain unresolved. always requires explicit human approval for each ready intent, spec, and plan. Omission uses auto.
reviewPolicy.title: Review policy

createPr.title: Open a pull request
createPr.description: Opt in to creating or updating a PR after review. Omission finishes locally. If a requested PR cannot be opened because no remote or credentials are available, report that limitation and finish locally.

nodes.prompt:
Resolve the configuration for this software change before planning or implementation.
Read the change request and repository instructions. Preserve the request text and supplied overrides.
If repoPath is supplied, resolve it to an absolute Git checkout path using the executing agent's working directory. Otherwise inspect the executing agent's current project and find its Git checkout. Do not infer the target from the Interlock server's working directory. If the target is missing or ambiguous, ask the person and wait for their answer before submitting this assignment.
Verify that the chosen Git checkout exists and is accessible to the executor. Read its artifact-directory convention.
If taskDir is supplied, use it after checking that it is relative to repoPath and remains inside the checkout, including through symlinks. Otherwise inspect existing task artifacts and run records for this request. Reuse an unambiguous matching task directory; if none matches, choose a descriptive outcome slug under .tasks/ unless repository guidance specifies another convention. Avoid collisions with unrelated tasks. Ask only when a material ambiguity remains.
If a matching active run already exists, report its ID and resume that run rather than duplicating its work. Do not cancel another run; ask the person how to handle this duplicate.
Record the resolved repoPath and taskDir in this assignment's result before drafting artifacts. Subsequent steps must use these exact values.
Use reviewPolicy auto when omitted and createPr false when omitted. Honor supplied values. Repository instructions and explicit human-review requests still apply under auto. PR creation requires createPr true and authorization; lack of a remote or credentials can be reported as local completion.
Do not implement, commit, open a PR, or create a new Git repository during setup.
Return repoPath, request, taskDir, reviewPolicy, and createPr.

context.instructions: Resolve setup from the supplied input and the executing agent's live project context. Verify paths and repository facts. Ask for an unresolved target instead of guessing. Never use the server's cwd as proof of the target project.

nodes.label: Draft intent
nodes.prompt:
Work in root.repoPath. Check that root.taskDir is a project-relative directory inside this Git repository.
Read the request and enough repository guidance to understand constraints. Preserve unrelated files.
Draft or revise root.taskDir/intent.md. This document owns the problem, desired outcome, affected users or systems, scope, constraints, and unresolved questions about intent. Record the source request and settled human decisions with their source.
Describe success at the outcome level. Leave detailed observable requirements and acceptance criteria to spec.md, and implementation steps and verification methods to plan.md.
On revision, apply the incoming feedback and retain settled decisions. Separate material decisions needing human input from technical questions the agent can investigate.
Keep draft changes uncommitted until this stage can proceed. Implementation starts after the plan can proceed.
Return artifactPath, summary, and openQuestions.

context.instructions:
Read root for repoPath, request, taskDir, and the effective reviewPolicy.
Read previous for the latest stage result or revision feedback. A policy envelope contains reviewPolicy and review; use previous.review as the stage result in that case.
An agent_review result with route proceed means progression under existing authorization. A human result with decision approved records explicit approval.
For revisions, apply feedback and preserve prior human decisions recorded in the artifacts and run. Ask again only about new material decisions.
Verify current repository facts and follow its instructions. Report blockers rather than inventing results.

source.description: Request passage or recorded prior human decision that authorizes the behavior.

feedback.description: Concrete corrections for revise. Empty for proceed.

nodes.prompt:
Read root.taskDir/intent.md and its source request and prior decisions. Check the problem, intended outcome, users, scope, and constraints against the original request and repository facts.
Check that intent.md defines intent clearly and leaves detailed behavior and acceptance criteria to spec.md, and implementation and verification methods to plan.md. Outcome-level success statements belong here.
Check cross-document references and any changed upstream decisions against their authoritative definitions and recorded authorization. Where earlier artifacts exist, check for contradictions, repeated definitions that could drift, and decisions placed in the wrong document. Brief orientation summaries are acceptable. Correct mechanical duplication or misplaced content through revise; escalate only when resolving the underlying decision needs human input.
Assess the artifact before choosing a route. Length or apparent detail alone does not establish authorization.
Return proceed when behavior and scope are settled, acceptance criteria follow from the request, and repository inspection reveals no conflict requiring a change to the requested outcome.
For proceed, provide concrete authorizationBasis entries and an empty decisions list. Record minor assumptions in the artifact. Report progression under existing authorization.
Return needs_human when a consequential product, scope, architectural, or policy decision is unresolved, when authorization conflicts, or when only the person can supply necessary information. Uncertainty about a material decision takes this route.
If the person explicitly requested human review of this stage, return needs_human with that approval question even when reviewPolicy is auto. List focused questions in decisions and explain why each matters. Cite the request and recorded decisions already available.
Return revise for corrections the agent can make from existing evidence. Supply located feedback. Investigate ordinary technical unknowns before escalating.
Preserve settled decisions. Review never invents a human approval. The graph separately enforces reviewPolicy always after proceed.
Leave implementation to the build stage. Return the output contract with decisionSource agent_review.

nodes.label: Draft spec
nodes.prompt:
On first entry to this stage, confirm intent.md can proceed. The incoming stage result, unwrapped from a policy envelope when present, must be agent_review with route proceed, or human with decision approved, and apply to the current intent artifact.
On a revision, previous is this spec stage's review feedback or human revision decision. Apply that feedback and preserve the already accepted intent and recorded authorization; do not treat this revision result as a new intent approval requirement. If feedback changes an upstream decision, follow the authorization and artifact ownership rules below.
Read the intent and relevant repository architecture, product, security, and UX guidance.
Before the first task commit, create or reuse the task branch under repository and harness conventions. Verify that it belongs to this task. Preserve unrelated changes and use a separate checkout when needed.
Record the task branch and exact full Git baseCommit in intent.md before committing any task artifact. For a resumed task, reuse its recorded original baseline and verify it against task history. Ask only if the task branch or baseline remains materially ambiguous.
Commit the accepted intent artifact to that task branch if still uncommitted.
Draft or revise root.taskDir/spec.md. This document owns required observable behavior, acceptance criteria, and the product or design decisions needed to define that behavior, including relevant alternatives, risks, and unresolved questions.
Give acceptance criteria stable identifiers such as AC1 and AC2. Preserve identifiers across revisions; do not renumber existing criteria.
For UI changes, include a brief UI proposal in spec.md before implementation. Describe the user flow, layout and action placement, relevant loading/empty/error/success states, keyboard and focus behavior, and narrow-screen behavior. Reuse the repository's existing components and interaction patterns. Cover only states the change affects; a short sketch or text is sufficient. Resolve consequential design choices through the existing spec review.
Reference intent.md for the problem, outcome, scope, and constraints instead of reproducing those definitions. Use relative links and specific headings or decision references where useful. Brief summaries that orient the reader are welcome; each decision or requirement has one authoritative definition.
Trace requirements to the request and prior human decisions. Flag conflicts or proposed changes to upstream decisions rather than silently redefining them here. Keep code areas, implementation sequence, and verification methods in plan.md.
On revision, apply feedback and retain settled human decisions with their source in the document that owns them. Keep references aligned when an authorized decision changes.
Keep the draft spec uncommitted until this stage can proceed. Return artifactPath, summary, and openQuestions.

nodes.label: Plan implementation
nodes.prompt:
On first entry to this stage, confirm spec.md can proceed. The incoming stage result, unwrapped from a policy envelope when present, must be agent_review with route proceed, or human with decision approved, and apply to the current spec artifact.
On a revision, previous is this plan stage's review feedback or human revision decision. Apply that feedback and preserve the already accepted spec and recorded authorization; do not treat this revision result as a new spec approval requirement. If feedback changes an upstream decision, follow the authorization and artifact ownership rules below.
Read intent.md, spec.md, current code, and repository instructions. Commit the accepted spec artifact to the task branch if still uncommitted. Preserve unrelated changes.
Draft or revise root.taskDir/plan.md. This document owns the implementation approach, intended code areas, implementation sequence, repository-specific tests and build or visual checks, implementation risks, and how completion will be demonstrated.
Map implementation steps and verification checks to the stable acceptance criterion identifiers in spec.md. Reference those criteria instead of copying their requirement text. Reference intent.md for scope and constraints. Use relative links and specific headings or decision references where useful.
Identify the change's highest-risk failure cases and pair each with a direct check and expected outcome. Choose cases from the actual change, such as missing references in each supported format/entry point, partial writes, stale responses, or a lost response after a successful mutation. A negative check must reach the claimed boundary and include a valid control; rollback checks compare complete protected state after an injected write failure.
Assign planned checks to build or independent review in plan.md. Build owns implementation tests and repository-required checks. Review owns independent diff review and targeted boundary verification. Completion and PR delivery belong to preparePr. Keep ownership in this existing plan; use existing output contracts and evidence rather than adding reports or roles.
For an interactive UI change, plan one short representative user journey through the changed behavior, with steps, expected visible results, and the relevant spec.md criterion identifiers. Choose interactions the change could affect, such as text entry, clipboard shortcuts, focus, save and reopen, or dragging; do not turn these examples into a universal checklist. For a copy-only or static visual change, a rendered inspection is sufficient. Non-UI changes need no UI journey.
Reuse existing interaction tests, automation, and verification evidence. A brief manual check through actual controls is acceptable. This workflow does not require new UI automation infrastructure or a separate UI verification document. Expand beyond the representative journey only for a concrete failure, uncovered required behavior, or broader impact from the change; record the reason.
Brief summaries that orient the reader are welcome; do not create a second authoritative definition of behavior, scope, or product decisions.
Distinguish verified repository facts from assumptions. Keep implementation choices within the authorized scope. Flag conflicts or proposed changes to upstream decisions rather than silently redefining them here.
On revision, apply feedback and retain settled human decisions with their source in the document that owns them. Keep references aligned when an authorized decision changes.
Keep the draft plan uncommitted until this stage can proceed. Return artifactPath, summary, and openQuestions.

nodes.prompt:
On the first build, confirm plan.md can proceed. The incoming stage result must be agent_review with route proceed, or human with decision approved, and apply to the current plan. A policy envelope contains review; use it as the stage result.
On a review revision, previous is the complete prior review result. Preserve the accepted plan and address every unresolved finding by its stable id, location, and details. Keep previous.baseCommit as the task baseline. Read the prior reviewed commit and inspect subsequent changes before fixing findings.
On the first build, verify and reuse the task branch and full baseCommit recorded in intent.md before the first task commit. Preserve this baseline on subsequent builds. For older task artifacts without a recorded baseline, establish the original task baseline from branch and PR history before proceeding. The current HEAD is not a substitute when it already contains task commits. If no reliable baseline can be established, report the blocker.
Commit the accepted plan artifact to the task branch if still uncommitted, preserving unrelated changes.
Implement the authorized change in root.repoPath. If new material decisions arise, pause for explicit human input and record it before dependent work.
Read the repository instructions and discover relevant tests, builds, formatting, documentation, and visual checks. On the first build, map each spec.md criterion identifier to an observable check or record the gap. Exercise relevant boundary states and inspect rendered UI behavior and copy when applicable.
Implement the spec's UI proposal and perform the plan's build-owned checks. Leave independent review and delivery to their existing stages. In checks.details, record criterion IDs, method, observed outcome, and an inspectable proof reference. For reused proof, keep its original commit and explain applicability to the current candidate. Inspect saved logs and snapshots for nonempty content, asserted outcomes, exit status, and evidence that the intended boundary was reached. Keep proof outside the checkout when saving it would change the candidate under review.
For interactive UI changes, exercise the planned representative journey through the actual controls. Use real clipboard operations, native shortcuts, focus changes, or gestures when those are the behavior being checked. Programmatically setting values or injecting state is useful for setup but does not establish that the corresponding user interaction works. For copy-only or static visual changes, inspect the rendered result.
Reuse existing interaction tests and evidence, or perform a brief manual check. Record the journey steps, expected and observed results, relevant criterion identifiers, verification method, and a concrete evidence reference in the existing checks details or plan.md. Do not add a separate UI report or build new automation infrastructure solely to satisfy this check.
Expand UI verification only for a concrete failure, uncovered required behavior, or broader impact from the change. On revisions, repeat only affected interactions or checks whose earlier evidence is no longer applicable. If the environment prevents an interaction check, record not_run with the limitation and affected criterion, leaving the verification gap explicit; do not claim it passed or spend open-ended effort provisioning tooling. Follow the existing blocker rules when that gap prevents verifying required behavior.
After fixes, rerun checks for each finding and affected behavior. Broaden verification when shared behavior, architecture, requirements, or changed dependencies could invalidate earlier results. Follow required repository checks. Do not rerun unrelated checks merely because another review iteration occurred.
Record exact check results and criterion identifiers, with any gaps. Do not weaken tests or claim an unexecuted check passed. Keep implementation and verification changes in plan.md; update an authorized decision in its owning artifact and align references.
Commit the intended code, tests, and affected docs according to repository practice. Return summary, branch, checks, baseCommit, and headCommit as full Git object IDs. headCommit must identify the commit containing all intended changes and artifacts submitted for review. Do not submit uncommitted task changes as reviewed work; preserve unrelated changes.
Do not merge or deploy. Report implementation or verification blockers with fail_work rather than submitting a success result.

nodes.prompt:
Review independently at previous.headCommit. Resolve the full Git object ID and confirm the branch and intended task changes match that commit. Inspect artifacts at the reviewed commit. Preserve unrelated working-tree changes; do not modify implementation. If intended changes or checks exist only in uncommitted files, return revise with a finding.
Use priorReview from the workflow input. It is null on the first review and contains the exact preceding review result on revisions. Record reviewedCommit, baseCommit, priorReviewedCommit, reviewScope, and scopeReason.
First review: use full scope. Verify the complete task diff from baseCommit to reviewedCommit against intent.md, spec.md, plan.md, and current repository rules. Inspect observable evidence for every spec.md acceptance criterion. A test count or implementer summary alone is insufficient. Exercise a relevant boundary state beyond the implementer's reported checks.
Use the plan's risks to choose that independent check. Inspect actual saved proof for nonempty content, asserted outcomes, exit status, and boundary reachability. Checking a criterion can use valid existing proof inspected independently; repeat execution only for affected behavior, unreliable proof, a material gap, or a concrete suspected failure. Attribute inspected proof accurately and retain its original commit. Missing proof is a verification gap, not proof of a product defect. Make a separate standards pass covering relevant regressions, security, documentation, UI behavior and copy, and deviations from the accepted plan.
Revision review: inspect the COMPLETE intervening diff from priorReview.reviewedCommit to reviewedCommit, including artifacts, tests, and unexpected edits. Assess its impact independently before choosing focused or full scope. Verify every prior outstanding finding and record a findingResolutions entry using its original id. Unresolved findings remain in findings with the same id; give new findings unique ids prefixed by the reviewed commit.
Use focused scope for localized corrections. Check the fixes, affected acceptance criteria, affected standards, and nearby regression risks. Exercise an additional boundary state when the changed behavior needs it; do not require a different unrelated boundary check each iteration.
Broaden to full scope when changes affect shared behavior or architecture, materially change requirements or accepted decisions, invalidate earlier evidence across the change, or leave the prior review baseline unreliable. Missing prior commits, history rewrites, or an inconsistent base require full review with an independently verified task baseline. If no reliable baseline can be established, report the blocker. Explain the scope decision; uncertainty about the impact requires full scope.
In either scope, return specEvidence for every current criterion using its stable identifier. For checked evidence, identify the actual check and commit. In focused scope, verified earlier evidence may be carried forward only after inspecting the entire intervening diff and explaining why it remains applicable. Preserve its original evidenceCommit and mark source carried_forward. Recheck affected criteria or mark unverified or gap. Full reviews check every criterion again and never carry evidence forward.
Return standardsEvidence with named checks, concrete references, evidenceCommit, and source. Apply the same rules to retaining unaffected standards evidence. Do not present earlier checks as newly executed checks.
For interactive UI changes, inspect the representative journey's evidence and confirm it exercises the actual controls and expected results. Direct value or state injection does not verify typing, clipboard shortcuts, focus, or gestures. Rendered inspection is sufficient for copy-only or static visual changes; non-UI changes need no UI journey.
Reuse valid captured interaction evidence. The existing independent boundary check can cover a relevant UI interaction; do not add another mandatory journey or repeat the entire journey merely because this is a review. Perform additional interaction checks only to resolve an evidence gap, investigate a concrete failure, or cover broader impact from the change. Attribute reported checks accurately; inspecting evidence does not mean you executed the interaction yourself.
Use existing tools or brief manual verification. Do not require new UI automation infrastructure or a separate report. Record blocked or missing interaction evidence against the affected criterion and apply the existing unverified/gap and verdict rules. On focused revisions, retain unaffected UI evidence under the same applicability and commit rules as other evidence.
Check that intent.md owns scope and constraints, spec.md owns behavior and acceptance criteria, and plan.md owns implementation and verification. Check references and recorded authorization for changed decisions; brief summaries are acceptable.
Return pass only when all material criteria are verified, all prior findings are resolved, affected standards pass, and no actionable findings remain. Otherwise return revise with located findings. Do not approve or merge a PR.

nodes.prompt:
Confirm the review verdict is pass. Verify the task branch HEAD equals previous.reviewedCommit and the intended task changes are committed. If the branch changed after review, report the blocker and require review of the new commit before finishing. A focused pass may combine newly checked evidence with explicitly retained evidence from earlier reviewed commits.
Verify the task branch contains root.taskDir/intent.md, spec.md, and plan.md and all intended code, tests, and docs. Check repository conventions and current branch status. Preserve unrelated changes.
Use the accepted review and applicable saved results for the final summary. Repeat checks only if delivery changes the candidate or repository instructions require them; a changed candidate still needs review.
When root.createPr is false, finish locally without creating or updating a PR. Return prUrl null and summarize the verified change, branch, checks, risks, and any plan deviations.
When root.createPr is true, create or update a PR for human review under existing authorization, linking the three artifacts and summarizing the change, checks run, unresolved risks, and any plan deviations. If a remote or credentials are unavailable, finish locally with prUrl null and state the delivery limitation. Do not invent a URL or report that a PR was opened.
Implementation or review failures still block completion. Local completion does not bypass review or verification. Do not merge or deploy.
Return taskDir, branch, prUrl, and summary.
